scenario: I generated a Moss & Moon discovery plan containing the marker BZ021-MOON-47. After refreshing the page, I asked AURA what the marker and task were. I had also observed that the conversation refreshed and there was no saved work for that chat.
observation: AURA said it could not access the earlier message and would not guess the marker or task. The related document was available in Documents, but the earlier conversation context was not.
severity: High — conversation continuity is a core part of continuing work.
user impact: The user may need to repeat work or may be unable to continue from the original conversation, even when a generated document still exists.
recommendation: Make chat saving and reopening behavior explicit. If chats are meant to persist, restore the conversation context after refresh; if documents and chats are saved separately, explain that distinction clearly.

scenario: I asked AURA for StudioFlow’s target market after earlier StudioFlow draft text had identified independent yoga studios.
observation: AURA said the target market was not stated in authorised Company DNA or supplied workspace evidence. It referred to the titles of the draft artifacts and said the titles did not establish a specific segment. However, the draft text shared during testing explicitly named independent yoga studios. This suggests a difference between draft-document content and the context AURA treats as authoritative; I cannot confirm the underlying retrieval behavior from the interface alone.
user impact: Users may have to re-enter known information, and may not know whether AURA can read a document’s content or only see its title.
recommendation: Show which sources AURA can actually use, distinguish draft documents from accepted Company DNA, and make source limitations explicit in the response.

scenario: I tried to archive a document from Documents.
observation: The action failed with Request failed with status code 503. The document remained in Documents and did not appear in the archive.
user impact: Users cannot rely on archiving to organise or remove a document from the active list.
recommendation: Fix the archive action and provide a clear success or failure state without leaving the user uncertain about the document’s status.

scenario: I looked for a way to delete a document in the Documents area.
observation: I could not find a delete option. I did not delete a document.
severity: Low to Medium; the intended product behavior and permissions are not clear.
user impact: Users may not know how to remove an unwanted document or whether archiving is the only option.
recommendation: Clarify whether deletion is supported, where it is available, and how it differs from archiving.

scenario: I tested the Documents library with 29 assets.
observation: Searching for StudioFlow returned 2 results. QA-S02 — StudioFlow — Interview Guide opened and its content was visible. After refresh, the document count remained 29. The category filter and return to All documents caused no issue in the checks reported.
user impact: No issue observed in these specific checks.
recommendation: No immediate change identified from this check. Timing and exhaustive verification of every document were not performed.

scenario: I provided founder-stated StudioFlow context through the Company DNA workflow, reviewed the generated draft, and attempted to approve and apply it.
observation: A 40% working draft appeared and remained after refresh; accepted Company DNA stayed at 0%. The approval was saved, but the final apply step failed. The same Finish applying recovery action returned the same failure again. The screen continued to show Approved / Final apply pending, and accepted version history said no proposal had completed the final apply step. The draft fields also contained AURA instructions such as “Show me a draft for review” and “Please record only these two product areas,” rather than only clean company facts.
severity: High — the final apply action is blocked for this update.
user impact: The user cannot complete an approved Company DNA update and is sent back into a recovery loop. If applied without correction, the draft would also place prompt instructions in Company DNA fields.
recommendation: Make the recovery action reliably complete the already-approved update without requiring a new approval. Keep the approved payload available, provide a clear cancel/edit route, and prevent prompt instructions from being stored as company facts.

scenario: I used the Company DNA voice flow, paused it, and resumed through Continue with AURA. I asked what AURA knew about StudioFlow.
observation: The interface showed Resume context — Saved · Paused and Continue with AURA. After resuming, AURA remembered class scheduling and membership management, but said the target market was not known. The later target-market response also showed that draft documents were not necessarily treated as authoritative memory. The voice interaction itself worked in the checks I made.
severity: Medium for context consistency; no voice-function failure observed.
user impact: Resuming is possible, but users may need to restate information that exists in a draft or that was provided in a different context.
recommendation: Make the source and scope of resumed context clear, and tell users whether voice resumes only within the live Voice session.

scenario: I checked Home recent work and the Company DNA page after generating and proposing StudioFlow information.
observation: Home showed recent-work items such as What is StudioFlow’s target market? and The company. Company DNA initially showed 0% accepted and no completed apply. Later it showed a 40% working draft; after approval, final application was still pending. The Company DNA screen describes accepted facts and proposed changes as separate states, but the distinction was initially unclear during testing.
severity: Low to Medium; the status is displayed, but the distinction was not immediately clear.
user impact: A user may assume that a Home item has updated Company DNA when it is only a saved work item or an unapplied proposal.
recommendation: Label Home items with their state (for example, saved work, pending Company DNA review, or accepted Company DNA) and link directly to the relevant review action.

scenario: Voice was used for the Company DNA workflow, but I did not run a separate, clean first-time-user guidance check.
observation: The user said the voice experience had been tested enough and was working, so no additional voice guidance test was performed.
user impact: No usability issue was reported; first-time guidance remains unverified.
recommendation: Only retest if the team still needs a dedicated first-time-user assessment.
